en.title: Nintendo Declares November 1st Pikmin Day With Surprise Direct
en.summary: Nintendo has officially declared November 1st as Pikmin Day, celebrating the charming strategy franchise with a surprise Nintendo Direct. The nearly ten-minute presentation offered fresh insights into the recently released Pikmin 4.
en.body:
In an unexpected move that caught many off guard, **Nintendo** has declared November 1st as **Pikmin Day**. This declaration was accompanied by a surprise Nintendo Direct presentation, dedicated entirely to Shigeru Miyamoto's beloved, bite-sized strategy series. The digital showcase, which ran for just over nine minutes, arrived on Halloween 2026, offering fans a delightful treat instead of spooky scares. While the Direct didn't feature a monumental **Pikmin 5** announcement or other earth-shattering news, it did provide valuable updates and a deeper look into the recently launched **Pikmin 4**.

Shigeru Miyamoto himself appeared in the Direct to explain the origins of **Pikmin Day**. Contrary to what many might expect, the date isn't tied to any specific game release. Instead, Miyamoto revealed that November 1st was chosen because the original three Pikmin, when placed side-by-side, visually resemble the numbers '11.1'. This quirky, creative reasoning underscores Nintendo's unique approach to celebrating its franchises, turning a simple visual gag into an official holiday. The franchise first launched in Japan in October 2001, with a North American release following in December of the same year, making the November 1st date a purely symbolic choice.

## Pikmin 4 Gets a Dandori Boost

The **Pikmin Day Direct** focused heavily on **Pikmin 4**, which recently launched on the **Nintendo Switch 2 Edition**. The presentation highlighted the game's intricate Dandori battles and offered a free demo for the **Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy**. This demo became available on November 2nd, allowing players to dive into the strategic gameplay and hone their Dandori skills. Miyamoto expressed his desire for more people to become familiar with the Pikmin universe, suggesting this day is just the beginning of increased attention for the series. He emphasized that going forward, his goal is to ensure that more players understand and appreciate the world of Pikmin, hinting at future content or initiatives.

## Fan Reaction and Community Engagement

The announcement of **Pikmin Day** and the accompanying Direct was met with a mix of amusement and genuine excitement from the **Pikmin** fan community. While some were taken aback by the somewhat arbitrary nature of the holiday, most appreciated Nintendo's dedication to a franchise that, while not as mainstream as Mario or Zelda, has a deeply passionate global following. The opportunity to receive new information and a demo for **Pikmin 4** on the **Nintendo Switch 2 Edition** provided a perfect way for fans to engage with the series. Many took to social media to share their plans for **Pikmin Day**, pledging to play their favorite titles on their **Nintendo Switch** or **Nintendo Switch 2** consoles, embracing the spirit of the newly established holiday and looking forward to more **Pikmin** content.

## What's Next for the Little Red Planet

With **Pikmin Day** now officially established, the future looks bright for the franchise. Nintendo has clearly signaled its intent to keep the **Pikmin** series in the spotlight, with Miyamoto's promise of increased focus. Fans can anticipate further updates on **Pikmin 4** and potentially new ways to experience the charming world of the tiny plant-like creatures. The free demo for **Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy**, available now, offers a substantial taste of the game's strategic depth.
